title: Callflow synthesis and contextual decisioning for soft failover
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Problem: We are seeing noisy paging during transient multi-region performance degradations where partial SLO breaches in noncritical routes cause full-team pages and manual cutovers. Goal: build an automated, context-aware triage layer that fuses SLO signals, request-level context, and regional health to (1) suppress noise, (2) invoke graded circuit-breaker actions (throttling / shed / local degrade), and (3) trigger contextual on-call guidance and automated mitigation playflows that can perform soft failover without an immediate human-driven global evacuation. This ticket implements the decisioning layer, runbook templates automation, and the integration glue to PagerDuty/Slack, runbook repo, and runtime metrics to enable canaries and gradual rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Signal fusion service ingests SLO burn-rate, 30s/5m error-rate deltas, and region health and produces a single contextual severity (low/medium/high/evacuate)
Noise reduction: total pages for transient 5-15m partial degradations reduced by >=60% in canary region compared to baseline

Circuit actions: system can autonomously apply a graded action (traffic throttle -> prioritized routing -> regional soft-failover) based on configured severity without manual approval when policy permits

On-call guidance: generated contextual incident cards (short summary, affected routes, suggested mitigation commands, rollback steps, and runbook links) are posted to on-call Slack channel and appended to PagerDuty incidents
Automated mitigation playflows exist for common failure modes (KV cache pressure, GC storms, autoscaler lag) and have end-to-end tests
Rollback/abort: a human on-call can abort automation and immediately revert to previous routing within 30s
Observability: dashboard displays decision inputs, chosen action, and pre/post SLO curves for the event window
implementation_notes: Architecture: lightweight signal-fusion microservice (Go) subscribes to metrics stream (Prometheus remote-write -> Kafka topic) and to tracing/context from X-Ray. Outputs actions to a control-plane queue consumed by runtime orchestrator.
Decisioning: use probabilistic scoring (0-1) combining normalized burn-rate, p50/p95 latency drift, and regional availability; thresholds tuned using historical incidents and simulated noise
Circuit model: three graded states - THROTTLE (soft shed by weight), DEGRADED_ROUTE (route-level local fallback), SOFT_FAILOVER (regional routing shift), with EVACUATE as manual escalation only
Runbook automation: canonical templates in /runbooks/auto/ generated from YAML parametrized stubs; automation writes incident cards to Confluence and links the generated runbook to PagerDuty incident
Controls: admin feature flag and per-customer opt-out for automatic mitigation; RBAC guarded endpoints for forced cutover
Safety: require double-confirmation for EVACUATE; all mitigation steps are reversible and logged to audit stream (KMS-signed events)
Testing harness: synthetic event generator replays historic SLO burn events and validates decision-to-action correctness; chaos tests will simulate partition and autoscaler lag
notes: 2026-02-24: Spec drafted during reliability guild. Initial framing: reduce noisy pages and enable safe automated soft-failover.
2026-02-26: PM review (Lena Ortiz) - emphasized customer-visible routes and per-customer opt-out; added requirement to avoid cascading global shifts for single-customer spikes.
2026-03-02: Design review - suggested probabilistic scoring and a short-term memory window (30s/5m/30m) to avoid oscillation. Design approved pending interface doc and security review.
2026-03-06: Security reviewed control-plane endpoints; recommended KMS signing for action tokens and per-action audit events. Security follow-up added.
2026-03-09: Implemented signal fusion prototype and local simulator. Early canary shows 52% reduction in pages for synthetic transients; thresholds need further tuning.
2026-03-12: Integrations PR opened for PagerDuty + Slack automation (PR #11234). Added automated incident card template and PagerDuty payload mapping. Planning canary in us-west-2 next week.
Notes: Keep human-in-loop for EVACUATE. Document training plans for on-call to understand new incident cards and automation behavior.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge prototype behind feature flag and enable metrics tagging
2) Internal canary: enable in staging and run synthetic event suite
3) Region canary: enable in us-west-2 for non-critical routes for 72h; monitor SLO and page volume
4) Expand to us-east-1 for a selected customer cohort with opt-in
5) Full rollout with gradual traffic weight increase and automatic threshold tightening
6) Post-rollout 2-week observation window and a retro
test_plan: Unit tests for scoring model and threshold transitions
Integration test: end-to-end flow from metric ingestion to runtime action (simulated Kafka -> control-plane queue -> runtime orchestrator)
Canary synthetic tests: replay historical incidents and confirm suppression rates and action correctness
Chaos tests: simulate partial region partition, autoscaler delay, and cold-start amplification
Manual runbook dry-run: on-call exercises triggered on staging incidents to validate incident card usefulness
metrics: Page volume reduction for transient events (target >=60%)
Mean time to mitigation (MTTM) for automated actions (target <60s to apply throttle)
False positive automation rate (target <1% of automations require rollback)
SLO burn reduction post-action (measured on affected routes)
Audit coverage: 100% of actions logged with signed events
risks: Risk of over-aggressive automation causing unnecessary regional shifts — mitigated via conservative initial thresholds and opt-out lists
Oscillation between degraded and normal states if thresholds are not hysteresis-aware — mitigated by multi-window scoring and minimum action hold-times
Operational complexity for on-call — addressed with concise incident cards and training
Security exposure of control-plane endpoints — KMS signing and RBAC required
Customer trust: need communication plan for customers who might observe degraded behavior during soft failovers
dependencies: ENG-654321 (KV cache eviction and memory-pressure telemetry)
